A1: Computer Fundamentals

SL: 11 hours | HL: 18 hours

Unit Overview

In this unit, you learn how a computer actually works at system level. You study CPU components and how they interact, the role of GPUs, different types of memory, the fetch–decode–execute cycle, storage, compression, operating systems, scheduling, control systems, and, at HL, translation processes such as interpretation and compilation.

Unit Objectives

What students are expected to know:

  • how the main CPU components work together
  • what GPUs do and how they differ from CPUs
  • how primary and secondary memory are used
  • how instructions move through the fetch–decode–execute cycle
  • how compression and cloud service models work
  • what operating systems do, including scheduling and resource management
  • how control systems operate
  • at HL, how interpreters and compilers translate code

Unit Outcomes

What students are expected to be able to do:

  • describe CPU components and the fetch–decode–execute cycle
  • explain the role of GPUs and compare them with CPUs
  • explain the purposes of different memory types
  • describe storage types, compression methods and cloud service models
  • describe and compare operating-system processes such as scheduling and interrupt handling
  • explain how control systems work in real-world contexts
  • at HL, evaluate interpreter and compiler translation processes

Subtopics

A1.1

Computer hardware and operation — CPU structure, GPU use, memory, storage, pipelining, compression and cloud services

 A1.2

Data representation and computer logic — binary and hexadecimal representation, stored data, logic gates, truth tables and logic diagrams

 A1.3

Operating systems and control systems — OS functions, scheduling, interrupts, multitasking, deadlock and control systems

 A1.4

Translation (HL only) — interpreters, compilers and translation approaches
